terms.comment: Our name, on the house pattern for toys (see toy version): massa, a soft lump, as of pitch or of cheese (Verg., Ov.), and in Church Latin dough. To shape it is fingere, the classical verb for modelling in wax or clay (fingere ē cērā, Cic. Verr. 2.4.30). Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for it.

evidence: Cic. Pis. 59: ex argillā et lutō fictus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: Let’s make a snake out of the play dough.

phrases.latin: Fingere ex argillā similitūdinēs Būtadēs Sicyōnius figulus prīmus invēnit Corinthī
phrases.english: Butades, a potter from Sicyon, was the first to model likenesses in clay, at Corinth

sources: Lewis & Short: massa · Lewis & Short: lusorius · Lewis & Short: argilla · Lewis & Short: fingo
